title: Double `/`, `//`, `%` by a scalar: a multiplication by the reciprocal
verdict: `rounding` of `divide` is not IEEE's where the divisor is a length-1 value against a longer column
description: With a length-1 divisor (a literal) against a column of two or more rows, Polars's in-memory engine computes `x / c` as `x * (1 / c)`: `49.0 / 49.0` is `0.9999999999999999`, and `0.0 / 1e-310` is NaN (`1 / 1e-310` is `inf`, and `0 * inf` NaN). `//` and `%` divide the same way. A column divisor of the same length divides as IEEE does. Here the streaming engine gave the IEEE quotient on four rows; the characterization pipeline's PL-3 reports it under streaming too.
reference: `divide` of doubles rounds the exact quotient (`TIE_TO_EVEN`), and `0.0 / c` is `0.0` for a finite nonzero `c`. The Polars translation broadcasts the divisor to a column (`column_divisor`).
